title: AI 16-Bit Pixel Art
description: Transforms the photo into authentic 16-bit console game pixel art.
positive_prompt: Transform the input photo into authentic 16-bit pixel art inspired by classic early-1990s console games. Recreate every subject, object, and background element using carefully placed square pixels, a controlled retro color palette, crisp pixel clusters, selective pixel outlines, stepped diagonal edges, and traditional dithering for shading. Use expressive sprite-like character rendering, readable silhouettes, stylized pixel-level facial details, and richly composed pixel-art environments. Maintain a consistent pixel grid and render with sharp nearest-neighbor scaling, without interpolation or blur. Rendering contract: Use the input image as visual ground truth. Treat the input image as the definitive reference. Keep the exact number of subjects and their left-to-right order, relative scale, pose, gaze, interaction, and key props. For every visible person, retain recognizable face geometry, recognizable identity as far as the pixel-art resolution permits, hairstyles, skin tone relationships, clothing colors, expressions, pose, gaze, proportions, and distinguishing features in a style-appropriate form; do not beautify, age, or swap identity unless explicitly requested. Keep the source camera angle, framing, background layout, and relative subject scale. Preserve the source aspect ratio. Apply the transformation consistently across the entire image to create one cohesive 16-bit game-art scene without inventing gameplay elements. Return one coherent finished image, not a before-and-after comparison, split screen, or unintended collage; output one static pixel-art image without game interfaces, health bars, dialogue boxes, readable text, letters, numerals, logos, signatures, or watermarks.
negative_prompt: smooth vector edges, anti-aliasing, blurry pixels, bilinear filtering, photorealism, 3D models, voxel art, low-effort pixelation filter, random pixel noise, inconsistent pixel sizes, excessive dithering, corrupted sprites, altered identity, missing subjects, extra people, incorrect body proportions, duplicated limbs, missing hands, changed clothing, HUD, score counters, text, logos, watermarks, split screen, identity drift, face swap, altered age, altered skin tone, wrong subject count, duplicated subject, merged subjects, inconsistent transformation, partial transformation, before-and-after, unintended collage, accidental crop, cut-off face, malformed anatomy, broken hands, fused fingers, extra limbs, incoherent perspective, floating objects, random text, gibberish letters, numerals, signature, interface elements
custom_prompt_placeholder: e.g. 16-bit RPG sprites, retro console palette...
